topicName: The Structure of the Earth and Major Landforms
description: An introduction to the internal structure of the earth, the continents and oceans, and the major landforms together with the earth movements that create them.

mcq.questionText: Which layer forms the outermost solid part of the earth on which we live?
mcq.explanation: The crust is the thin, solid outer layer of the earth where all life and landforms are found.

mcq.questionText: Which layer of the earth lies directly below the crust and is the thickest layer?
mcq.explanation: The mantle lies beneath the crust and is the thickest of the three main layers of the earth.

mcq.questionText: The innermost layer of the earth is mainly made up of which metals?
mcq.explanation: The core of the earth is composed mainly of the metals iron and nickel.

mcq.questionText: Which part of the earth's core is in a liquid (molten) state?
mcq.explanation: The outer core is in a liquid or molten state, while the inner core is solid because of the very high pressure.

mcq.questionText: How many continents are found on the earth?
mcq.explanation: The earth has seven continents: Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Australia and Antarctica.

mcq.questionText: Which is the largest ocean on the earth?
mcq.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on the earth.

mcq.questionText: Tanzania borders which ocean to its east?
mcq.explanation: The Indian Ocean lies along the eastern coast of Tanzania and the rest of East Africa.

mcq.questionText: A large, raised area of land with a fairly flat or level top is called a:
mcq.explanation: A plateau is an elevated area of land with a flat or gently undulating top, often called a tableland.

mcq.questionText: Which landform is formed when layers of rock are bent or buckled by compression forces?
mcq.explanation: When rock layers are squeezed by compression forces they bend upward and downward to form fold mountains.

mcq.questionText: The upward bend or arch formed during folding of rocks is called a/an:
mcq.explanation: An anticline is the upfold or arch in folded rocks, while the downfold or trough is called a syncline.

mcq.questionText: A crack or break in rocks of the crust along which movement takes place is called a:
mcq.explanation: A fault is a fracture in the crustal rocks along which the rocks move up, down or sideways.

mcq.questionText: The Great Rift Valley that passes through Tanzania was mainly formed by the process of:
mcq.explanation: The Rift Valley was formed when the crust faulted and the central block sank between two parallel faults.

mcq.questionText: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is an example of which type of landform?
mcq.explanation: Mount Kilimanjaro was formed by volcanic activity, making it a volcanic mountain.

mcq.questionText: The opening on the earth's surface through which lava and gases escape during a volcanic eruption is called the:
mcq.explanation: A vent is the central pipe or opening through which magma, lava and gases reach the earth's surface.

mcq.questionText: A low, flat or gently sloping area of land is best described as a:
mcq.explanation: A plain is an extensive area of low, flat or gently sloping land, often good for farming.

fib.questionText: The three main layers of the earth are the crust, the mantle and the _____.
fib.explanation: The core is the innermost layer of the earth, surrounded by the mantle and the crust.

fib.questionText: The thin, solid outermost layer of the earth is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The crust is the layer on which the continents and oceans rest.

fib.questionText: The earth's core is made up mainly of the metals iron and _____.
fib.explanation: Iron and nickel are the main metals that make up the inner and outer core.

fib.questionText: The largest ocean on the earth is the _____ Ocean.
fib.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of all the oceans.

fib.questionText: The coldest continent on the earth, found around the South Pole, is _____.
fib.explanation: Antarctica is the southernmost continent and is covered by a thick layer of ice.

fib.questionText: An elevated area of land with a flat top is known as a _____.
fib.explanation: A plateau is a highland area with a fairly level surface, also called a tableland.

fib.questionText: Mountains formed when rock layers are bent by compression are called _____ mountains.
fib.explanation: Fold mountains form where compressional forces buckle the crustal rocks into folds.

fib.questionText: The process by which rocks crack and move along fractures in the crust is called _____.
fib.explanation: Faulting involves the breaking and displacement of rocks along lines of weakness called faults.

fib.questionText: The long depression formed by faulting that runs through East Africa is called the Great _____ Valley.
fib.explanation: The Great Rift Valley is a large faulted depression stretching through East Africa, including Tanzania.

fib.questionText: Molten rock that flows out onto the earth's surface during a volcanic eruption is called _____.
fib.explanation: Magma that reaches the surface and pours out during an eruption is known as lava.

tf.questionText: The crust is the thickest layer of the earth.
tf.explanation: The crust is the thinnest layer; the mantle is the thickest of the three main layers.

tf.questionText: The inner core of the earth is solid because of the very high pressure acting on it.
tf.explanation: Although it is extremely hot, the intense pressure keeps the inner core in a solid state.

tf.questionText: Africa is one of the seven continents of the earth.
tf.explanation: Africa is the continent in which Tanzania is located and is one of the seven continents.

tf.questionText: The Indian Ocean lies along the western coast of Tanzania.
tf.explanation: The Indian Ocean lies along the eastern coast of Tanzania, not the western side.

tf.questionText: A plain is a high area of land with steep slopes and a flat top.
tf.explanation: A plain is a low, flat or gently sloping area of land, not a high area with steep slopes.

tf.questionText: Fold mountains are formed by compression forces that bend layers of rock.
tf.explanation: Compression squeezes rock layers and bends them into upfolds and downfolds, forming fold mountains.

tf.questionText: A fault is a fracture in the rocks of the crust along which movement can occur.
tf.explanation: Faults are breaks in the crust along which rocks shift up, down or sideways.

tf.questionText: The Great Rift Valley was formed mainly by the deposition of river sediments.
tf.explanation: The Rift Valley was formed by faulting, when a block of land sank between two parallel faults.

tf.questionText: Volcanicity involves the movement of magma from inside the earth towards or onto the surface.
tf.explanation: Volcanicity is the process by which magma rises through the crust and may erupt as lava at the surface.

tf.questionText: Mount Kilimanjaro was formed by folding of rock layers.
tf.explanation: Mount Kilimanjaro is a volcanic mountain formed by volcanic activity, not by folding.

summary.questionText: The three main layers of the earth
summary.correctAnswer: The crust, the mantle and the core.
summary.explanation: Moving from the outside inwards, the earth is made up of the crust, the mantle and the core.

summary.questionText: The outermost layer of the earth
summary.explanation: The crust is the thin, solid layer on which we live.

summary.questionText: Main metals making up the earth's core
summary.explanation: Both the inner and outer core are made mostly of iron and nickel.

summary.questionText: Number of continents on the earth
summary.explanation: They are Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Australia and Antarctica.

summary.explanation: Squeezing of rock layers produces upfolds and downfolds that build fold mountains.

summary.questionText: How the Rift Valley was formed
summary.correctAnswer: By faulting, with a block of land sinking between two faults.
summary.explanation: The central block subsided between parallel faults to form the long rift depression.

summary.questionText: Example of a volcanic mountain in Tanzania
summary.explanation: Mount Kilimanjaro was built up by volcanic activity.

hoq.questionText: A student observes that Tanzania has both Mount Kilimanjaro and the Great Rift Valley with its lakes. Which conclusion best explains why these two very different landforms occur in the same region?

options.text: Both were formed only by river deposition over many years
The region experiences earth movements, where faulting created the rift while volcanicity built the mountain
Both landforms were created by folding of rock layers
The landforms have no connection to forces inside the earth

hoq.explanation: East Africa is a zone of active earth movements, so faulting produced the Rift Valley while related volcanicity built up volcanic mountains like Kilimanjaro.

hoq.questionText: Scientists cannot dig down to study the inner core directly, yet they state it is made of iron and nickel and is very hot. Why is the inner core solid rather than liquid despite the extreme heat?

options.text: Because the enormous pressure deep inside the earth keeps it solid
Because the inner core is actually cold compared with the crust
Because iron and nickel can never melt at any temperature
Because the crust cools the inner core directly

hoq.explanation: The pressure at the centre of the earth is so great that it keeps the iron and nickel of the inner core in a solid state even at very high temperatures.

hoq.questionText: A farmer is choosing land for growing crops and compares a steep, rocky plateau edge with a wide, gently sloping plain near a river. Which area is generally more suitable for farming and why?

options.text: The plateau edge, because steep slopes hold more water
The plain, because flat low land with river soils is easier to cultivate and more fertile
Neither, because all landforms are equally poor for farming
The plateau edge, because its rocky surface improves crop growth

hoq.explanation: Plains are low, flat or gently sloping and often have fertile soils deposited by rivers, making them easier to farm than steep, rocky plateau edges.
